subject: Recap: Bellwether performance qualification + proposed levers
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lin <kate@bellwether.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: Bellwether performance qualification + proposed levers

Hi Kate — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps for qualification. I pulled out the points we flagged and sketched the levers we think will get you to your latency/throughput goals without blowing up cost.

Summary of your targets (from call):
- Primary SLO: p95 tail for interactive assistant flows <= 180 ms (goal: 150 ms)
- Typical payload: ~450 tokens request + ~120 tokens response (avg)
- Streaming: partial-response streaming required for chat UX (must start sending within ~50-80 ms of generation)
- Peak concurrency: ~260 concurrent sessions, expected sustained QPS ~90, peak bursts to ~170 for short windows
- Availability requirement: 99.9% during business hours (US)

Key cost / performance levers (what Redwood will evaluate in the perf lab):
1) Continuous batching with deadline-aware routing — pack short waiting windows to amortize GPU kernel overhead while keeping latency SLOs.
2) KV/prefix caching for repeated context in sessions (reduces per-request compute for warm sessions).
3) Quantization profiles: evaluate 4-bit vs 8-bit for the 7B and 13B family to trade compute vs output fidelity.
4) Model variants & fallbacks: baseline = 7B-q4 for typical assistant queries, fallback to 13B-fp16 only for high-quality generation or long-context paths.
5) Streaming micro-batching: pipeline first-token stream while batching subsequent tokens to reduce p95.
6) Concurrency shaping + graceful degradation: limit per-session concurrency and serve degraded non-streaming cards when system is overloaded.

Proposed qualification plan (high level):
- You upload a ~24h sample trace (or representative trace slice) containing request sizes, timing, and session continuity — we can use it to synthesize a load test. (Attachment requested: bellwether_sample_trace.json)
- Redwood runs a 2-day perf lab with 3 profile runs: baseline (no quant), q4-profile, q8-profile, streaming enabled/disabled permutations. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost-per-1M-tokens.
- Post-run: 1-page recommendation that maps your target p95 -> recommended model/quant/policy + expected unit cost and expected monthly cost range for your projected QPS.

Immediate asks / next steps for Bellwether:
- Please share the sample trace (or a CSV of request sizes + timing) and a short list of 3 representative prompts (sensitive data redacted).
- Confirm whether streaming start latency (time-to-first-byte) target is strict for all requests or only for interactive sessions.

Internal ask (cc'd): Lauren/Neha — want to align lab capacity and preliminary model mapping before we ingest traces. Lauren, can you spin up a 4-8 hour slot on perf lab (GPUs: A100 or H100) and pick two candidate model images (a 7B quant and a 13B fp16)? Neha — please prepare the cost calculator sheet so we can hand Kate expected $/1M token bands.

Attachments: redwood_perf_plan_v1.pdf (proposal), sample trace placeholder requested: bellwether_sample_trace.json

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a short kickoff once we have the trace.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Kate Lin <kate@bellwether.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Bellwether AI Technical <eng@bellwether.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 18:03:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Bellwether performance qualification + proposed levers

Thanks Priyom — that lines up with what we took away. Appreciate the clear plan.

I attached a 6-hour representative trace and a CSV summary of request sizes and timestamps (bellwether_sample_trace.json, bellwether_load.csv). The upload is redacted for PII. A few clarifications:
- Streaming start latency goal should be strict for interactive chat sessions only (not for bulk async batch jobs).
- For interactive flows, typical response length is closer to 90–140 tokens (we rounded up on the call).
- During peak promo events we can see short bursts to ~200 QPS for ~5–10 minutes, but sustained QPS is ~80–110.

We’re happy to run a short protective QA window if you need to test with production-like keys. Let us know what you need from our side and which time windows work for the perf lab.

On the pilot model question: we’re comfortable starting with a 7B-quantized candidate if latency wins are material, but want to validate output quality on 500 samples.

Kate
Kate Lin
Head of Product
Bellwether AI

Attachments: bellwether_sample_trace.json (6.3MB stub), bellwether_load.csv (12KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Bellwether performance qualification + proposed levers

Nice recap, Priyom — I’ll take the perf lab lead on this. Proposed runbook:
1) Day 0: ingest trace, sanity-check payloads, synthesize minor variations (token lengths + short bursts).
2) Day 1 morning: run baseline runs (7B fp16, 13B fp16) streaming disabled to get raw per-token throughput.
3) Day 1 afternoon: enable streaming + continuous batching (deadline 20 ms) runs.
4) Day 2: evaluate q4 profile with the same scheduling and run a 500-sample quality check vs your golden set (Bellwether provides).
5) Deliverable: p50/p95/p99 table, cost bands, recommended config + fallback map.

Capacity: I have two H100 slots open Tue/Wed 13:00–17:00 UTC — would that cover the burst scenarios Kate mentioned? If not we can use A100 for longer runs.

Neha — can you draft the initial cost bands using the redwood_perf_plan_v1 template (attached) so we have numbers for the kickoff?

-Lauren

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lin <kate@bellwether.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Bellwether performance qualification + proposed levers

Perfect — thanks all. Quick confirmation and actions:
- Kate: we got the trace & CSV, thanks. We’ll use the H100 window Tue/Wed 13:00–17:00 UTC per Lauren.
- Lauren: runbook approved. Please prioritize the streaming micro-batching runs first on Day 1.
- Neha: draft cost bands & 3 scenario estimates (conservative / expected / optimistic) by EOD Tue so we can share during the kickoff.
- Deliverable timing: initial perf summary within 48 hours of runs finishing; final one-pager + recommended config within 5 business days.

Links: HubSpot deal record + kickoff calendar: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/BW-2026-1093

I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff right now and include the perf lab run slots. Kate — once you accept the invite we’ll mark the trace as ingested.

Thanks — looking forward to proving we can hit 150–180 ms p95 while keeping unit cost tight.

—Priyom
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
